status_note: active but strategically superseded: README now says 'This is the open-source visual editor that started Onlook (Next.js + Tailwind). The hosted product we're building next ... is in early access via the waitlist' — the OSS web app is the legacy product, 382 open issues, last substantive commit in clone 2026-07-21. Fully open (Apache-2.0) but operationally dependent on external services: CodeSandbox SDK (sandboxes), Supabase (auth/db), OpenRouter (LLMs), Morph/Relace (fast-apply), Freestyle (hosting), PostHog, Langfuse. Self-hosting docs exist (docker-compose). apps/admin is a git submodule to a separate repo. Next.js + Tailwind projects only.
core_problem: Let designers edit a real Next.js codebase visually: every DOM edit in a live preview (style, text, insert, move, group) is translated into an AST edit of the exact JSX source that produced that element, with an AI chat that has the same code access.
architecture: Monorepo (Bun). apps/web/client is a Next.js app whose state is a MobX EditorEngine (components/store/editor/engine.ts) composed of managers: branches (each branch = its own sandbox + history + CodeFileSystem), frames (iframes on an infinite canvas), elements/overlay/snap (selection UI), action, history, code, ast, style, text, insert, move, group, copy, image, font, theme, pages, chat, git, sandbox, screenshot, ide. The user's project runs inside a CodeSandbox VM (packages/code-provider: CodesandboxProvider | NodeFsProvider) and is mirrored into a browser-side CodeFileSystem (packages/file-system) by a sync engine. DOM<->source mapping ('sourcemap for JSX'): CodeFileSystem.writeFile -> processJsxFile parses with @babel/parser (ts+jsx), addOidsToAst (packages/parser/src/ids.ts) stamps data-oid="" on every JSXOpeningElement except Fragments, deduping against per-file/global/branch OID sets (conflicts or duplicates get fresh ids), regenerates with retainLines:true, prettier-formats, and rebuilds an index oid -> JsxElementMetadata { path, branchId, startTag/endTag {line,column}, component (enclosing function/class/variable name via a componentStack), dynamicType: array|conditional (detected from .map() callbacks, ternaries, &&/||), coreElementType: component-root|body-tag, code (exact source slice) } via createTemplateNodeMap + getContentFromTemplateNode (packages/parser/src/template-node/map.ts); the index is persisted and rebuildIndex batches all JSX files. core_innovation: A write-time 'source map for JSX' (stable data-oid stamped into source, indexed to file/line/column/enclosing-component/dynamic-context) that lets non-destructive DOM edits be replayed as inverse-safe serializable actions which are compiled into AST edits of the originating source.
strengths: Cleanest open implementation of DOM->source mapping: stable ids injected at write time (not build time), a persisted oid index with exact ranges and enclosing component, and explicit handling of dynamic contexts (.map, ternaries) and component-instance vs definition.

Serializable inverse actions with transactions (packages/models/src/actions, store/editor/history): every edit is data, undo is computed not snapshotted, continuous edits coalesce, and the docs state the intent that 'an agent generate actions'.

Non-destructive live preview: style edits live in an injected stylesheet keyed by DOM ids (css-tree AST) and text edits in an overlay, so nothing in the app is mutated until the action is committed to code.
Typed RPC boundary between editor and page (penpal; PenpalChildMethods = typeof preloadMethods) with reconnect logic — a small, reviewable contract instead of ad-hoc postMessage.

Layer tree is derived from the real DOM (buildLayerTree) then enriched from source metadata (component name, dynamic/conditional flags) — the editor tells users when an element is one of many rendered by a loop.
Tool-call repair via a small model constrained to the tool's Zod schema; ASK/EDIT/CREATE/FIX modes with distinct prompts and models; summary-mode context compaction.
Apache-2.0, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md present (repo is agent-friendly), branches-as-sandboxes and git checkpoints give cheap experiment/rollback semantics.
weaknesses: Product pivot: the OSS repo is now the predecessor of a hosted product; expect slowing maintenance (382 open issues) and no roadmap for non-Next.js/non-Tailwind support.
Heavy external-service coupling (CodeSandbox SDK, Supabase, OpenRouter, Morph/Relace, Freestyle, PostHog, Langfuse); the web app is not a library you can embed — it is a whole SaaS clone.

data-oid attributes are written into the user's source files and shipped to production DOM unless stripped (removeIdsFromAst exists but is opt-in); LLM prompts must be told not to touch them; regenerate+prettier can produce noisy diffs.
Style edits are lossy: CSS deltas are translated to Tailwind classes (CssToTailwindTranslator) — anything Tailwind cannot express is dropped or approximated; non-Tailwind projects unsupported.

Instance resolution is a heuristic (N-th same-named child in the parent's source slice) that degrades under conditionals/maps; real-time insert is disabled as buggy; undo requires a code write + HMR round trip (slow, and a failed write desynchronises DOM and source).
Babel-specific pipeline (JSX AST, retainLines codegen) — no path to .astro templates without a different parser/serializer.
The editing model is 'edit arbitrary source' — the opposite of a typed SiteDefinition; there is no schema, no catalogue, no constraints on what the designer or AI may change.
Security posture of the preload channel is permissive (allowedOrigins '*', TODO in source).
patterns_to_steal: Inverse serializable Action union with Change<T>{original, updated} and transactions -> visual_editor over SiteDefinition: define SiteEditAction (set-copy, swap-asset, reorder-section, toggle-section) with computed inverses and coalescing; history is the action log, which doubles as telemetry input.

Write-time stable node ids + persisted id index (oid -> file/range/component/dynamic flags) -> renderer/visual_editor: stamp data-section-id / data-node-path from the SiteDefinition into rendered Astro output so the preview can map any click back to a Zod path; Astro dev mode already emits data-astro-source-file/loc for the code-first case (verify).

Non-destructive preview stylesheet keyed on DOM ids (css-tree managed) -> visual_editor: preview owner edits (e.g. design_system swap, copy) as an overlay before committing a new SiteDefinition version.
Typed penpal RPC contract between editor and preview iframe -> visual_editor: one exported preloadMethods object whose type is the contract; keep the page-side script dependency-free.

Layer tree from DOM enriched with source metadata (dynamic/conditional markers) -> visual_editor: show owners which elements are repeated from data (fact lists, testimonials) so they edit the source record, not one instance.

Tool-call repair with a schema-constrained small model -> agent_orchestration: when the selection model emits an invalid design_system_id/arrangement payload, repair against the Zod schema instead of retrying the big model.
Branch = sandbox + git checkpoints -> agent_orchestration/qa_gate: run alternative arrangements as branches with checkpoints so the QA gate can compare and roll back deterministically.
Separate CREATE/EDIT/ASK/FIX prompt+model routing with stepCountIs limits -> agent_orchestration: bound tool loops per stage.
patterns_to_avoid: Editing arbitrary source AST as the owner-facing model -> owners edit typed fields of SiteDefinition; sections are human-authored and immutable to owners; only the agency pipeline (and only via section variants) changes layout.
CSS -> Tailwind class translation of free-form style edits -> styles come from selected design tokens; there is no free style editing to translate.
Injecting editor ids into committed source files -> ids belong to the rendered output/SiteDefinition, never to the authored section templates.
CREATE-from-prompt page generation and fast-apply file rewriting -> rejected generation path; our model selects ids, it does not write section code.
Depending on a hosted sandbox (CodeSandbox) for preview -> Astro dev server or a static build in a local worker is sufficient and deterministic.
reusable_patterns: SourceIdSourcemap: stamp a stable id attribute on every authored element at write time and keep an index id -> {file, range, enclosing component, dynamic context} so any rendered node maps back to its source.
InverseActionHistory: edits are serializable actions with a pure inverse function; undo/redo re-dispatch computed inverses; transactions coalesce continuous edits.
OverlayStylesheetPreview: preview changes as rules in a dedicated injected stylesheet keyed by per-node ids, leaving the application's own styles untouched until commit.
InstanceVsDefinitionResolution: when a source element renders multiple DOM nodes, resolve each node to the usage site (instance id) by walking to the nearest component boundary.
TypedIframeRPC: a single exported methods object on the page side whose TypeScript type is the contract, bridged with a promise-based messenger with reconnect.
SchemaConstrainedToolRepair: on invalid tool arguments, ask a small model to regenerate them against the tool's schema before failing.
adoption_strategy: Adapt — Onlook is the wrong product shape for owners (arbitrary source editing, Next.js/Tailwind only, SaaS-tethered, pivoting) but the right mechanics for a code-aware editor and for the agent loop. Immediately: define SiteDefinition edits as an inverse-action union with transactions (their HistoryManager/helpers are ~300 lines and portable), and stamp SiteDefinition node ids into Astro output so the future editor can map DOM->Zod path without any Babel machinery. Post-V1 editor: reuse the penpal-style typed RPC + overlay-stylesheet preview over an Astro dev iframe; skip CodeSandbox, Tailwind translation and AST rewriting. For the agency's internal code-first loop (agent fixes a section arrangement), Astro's dev-mode source-location attributes replace data-oid; only if we need programmatic .astro rewrites would we build an @astrojs/compiler-based equivalent of packages/parser (difficulty ~6). Do not run the app itself.
